item.title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It
item.description: A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access to a locked Windows computer start programs without signing in. Whoever uses it gets only a limited account, not administrator control of the machine. The method was posted yesterday by a researcher who uses the handles MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse , and the endpoint-security firm ThreatLocker tested it the same day and found it works. There is no fix from Microsoft yet, and nothing shows the method has been used in a real attack. The technique does not work on every machine. It requires physical access to the computer and a Microsoft account accessible through the lock screen's recovery options, and it uses Windows' built-in screen reader, Narrator, to navigate the locked screen. item.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
item.description: PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server. Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell . The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 and rated 9.2 out of 10 on the CVSS 4.0 scale by PHP's maintainers. Depthfirst, a security company, says it found the flaw and reported it to the maintainers. The October 21 PHP releases, which fixed two critical flaws known as PHP2Shell , do not contain this fix. Servers updated then remain affected until they install today's releases. Neither the maintainers nor the company reports any attacks using phpAfterShell. item.title: Critical VMware vCenter Zero-Day Flaw Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
item.description: A critical flaw in VMware vCenter lets an attacker with network access bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system, Broadcom, which owns VMware, said in an advisory published today. Fixed versions are out for all supported branches, and the company lists no workaround. vCenter is the central console for managing an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-123890 and is rated 9.8 on the CVSS scoring system. "VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service," the advisory says. In an FAQ published with the advisory, the company says the issue "qualifies under ITIL methodologies as an emergency change," and urges organizations to consult their security staff immediately on timing. The flaw was exploited as a zero-day more than two months before the patch, Google's threat intelligence team said in a technical analysis published November 2...

item.title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
item.description: Under specific conditions, a critical vulnerability in Drupal core can allow an attacker without login credentials to use the built-in installer to attempt to reinstall a site. That can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution, and the project rates the vulnerable configurations as uncommon. Fixed releases for all supported branches shipped yesterday. The Drupal Security Team disclosed the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-132165, yesterday and rated it critical, 18 out of 25 on the project's risk scale. The installer ships in every copy of Drupal core as the file /core/install.php and stays on the site after installation. Core's default .htaccess rules do not block requests to it, so blocking it is left to each site. No attacks are reported in the security advisory , which rates exploitation as complex and records an existing proof-of-concept exploit. item.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
item.description: One of the early targets of PHP2Shell exploitation was the firewall. On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting the two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws let anyone execute code on the web server without authentication. The disclosure itself went a little wrong. Details leaked on October 20, ahead of the coordinated release, and the PHP project shipped an emergency patch the next day. The vulnerabilities require no authentication, but they are not easy to exploit reliably. It takes skill and additional knowledge about the target system. Where it matters a lot is appliances, which run identical, often outdated software that an attacker can study in advance. That is the bigger picture. item.title: Ruby Ships Fixes for 7 Flaws, Including Critical Ruby2Shell, Said to Hit Default Rails Apps Pre-Auth
item.description: Ruby contains seven memory-safety flaws in its regular expression engine and its string case-conversion code. For five of them, its maintainers say, proof-of-concept exploits, or PoCs, have shown that crafted input can run code on the machine. "We are aware of PoCs that prove some of them can be used to trigger remote code execution," the maintainers said. The project released fixed versions yesterday: Ruby 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14. Whether an application is at risk depends on whether an attacker can get crafted patterns or strings into the affected code, and the advisories report no attacks so far. The other two flaws are weaker. The maintainers say one has proof-of-concept code that corrupts memory under an attacker's control but has not been shown to run code, and the other can only read memory it should not or crash the program. The project set the seven out in a security announcement and a separate advisory for each. The advisories rate three flaws critica...

item.title: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
item.description: Low-privilege database accounts that cannot read a single application table can still be used to run code on the database server itself, a researcher has shown, by reaching memory-corruption bugs in the engine code behind ordinary SQL. The exploits, published yesterday, are the researcher's proofs of concept against PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus a separate Oracle chain that needs no login. None has been seen in a real attack. The work is by Zheng Yu , a researcher at Depthfirst . A database account's SQL permissions control which tables and schemas it can access, the researcher argues, not the memory-unsafe C and C++ code the engine runs to read, plan, and execute a query. Common grants give an account enough room to reach that code. PostgreSQL's default TEMPORARY privilege, or the right to create temporary tables in MySQL and ClickHouse, allows an account to create objects or send input that triggers a memory bug.
